title: The Last Passenger
text: It was almost midnight when Rakib left his friend's house and started walking toward the old bus station in Old Dhaka. The streets were unusually quiet that night. Most of the shops were closed, and the yellow streetlights were flickering as if they were about to go out. Rakib checked his phone. It was 11:45 PM. He knew the last bus usually arrived around midnight, so he decided to wait. After nearly twenty minutes, he heard the sound of an engine coming from far away. An old bus slowly appeared through the darkness. Its headlights were weak, and several windows were broken. Rakib waved at the driver and climbed inside. The bus was completely empty except for an old man sitting in the last seat. Rakib chose a seat near the front and tried not to look back. After a few minutes, the old man suddenly spoke. 'Do you remember me?' Rakib felt uncomfortable but turned around anyway. The old man's face looked strangely familiar. He looked exactly like Rakib's father, who had died five years earlier. Rakib's hands began to shake. He stood up and asked, 'Who are you?' The old man smiled and said, 'You used to sit beside me when you were a child.' Suddenly, all the lights inside the bus went out. Rakib closed his eyes and started praying. After a few seconds, the lights came back on. The old man was gone. Rakib immediately ran toward the driver and asked what had happened. The driver looked at him through the mirror and said, 'What are you talking about? There has been no passenger in the back seat.' Rakib looked behind him. The seat was empty. But there was something lying on it—a small photograph of Rakib as a child, sitting beside his father. On the back of the photograph was a handwritten message: 'I am still waiting for you.'

location: The Bank of the Padma River, Rajshahi
title: The Voice from the Other Side
text: Suman often went to the bank of the Padma River whenever he needed some peace and quiet. One winter night, he decided to go there alone after finishing his work. The sky was dark, and a thick layer of fog covered the river. There were no boats, no fishermen, and no people nearby. Suman sat on the ground and listened to the sound of the water. At exactly 2:13 AM, he heard someone whisper his name from across the river. 'Suman...' He immediately stood up and looked toward the opposite bank. At first, he could not see anything because of the fog. Then the voice came again, louder this time. 'Suman, come here.' He noticed a human-shaped figure standing in the middle of the river. The figure was wearing a long white dress, and its hair was hanging over its face. Suman knew it was impossible for anyone to stand there because the water was deep. Still, he took a few steps toward the river. The figure slowly raised its hand and waved at him. Suman felt as if something was pulling him toward the water. He was about to step into the river when he suddenly heard his friend's voice behind him. 'Suman! Don't go any closer!' Suman turned around and saw his friend standing several meters away. His friend was breathing heavily as if he had been running. 'Why are you here?' Suman asked. His friend looked terrified and replied, 'I received a phone call from your number. You were screaming for help.' Suman checked his phone. There were no outgoing calls. Then both of them looked toward the river. The figure was gone. They quickly started walking away. After a few seconds, Suman heard a whisper directly behind his ear. 'You came so close...' He turned around, but nobody was there. When they reached home, Suman's friend showed him his phone. There was a new voice recording on it. The recording contained Suman's voice saying, 'I am still at the river. Please come and find me.'

title: The Locked Room
text: In a small village, there was an old two-story house that had been abandoned for many years. The house belonged to an elderly man who had moved away after the death of his wife. The villagers avoided the house because strange things happened there every night. People often heard footsteps coming from the second floor, even though nobody lived there. Some villagers also claimed that a woman could sometimes be seen standing behind the window of a locked room. Nobody knew why the room was locked. One night, Raihan and his friends decided to investigate the house. They entered around midnight with flashlights and cameras. The first floor was covered with dust. Old furniture was lying everywhere, and several family photographs were hanging on the walls. When they reached the second floor, they found the mysterious room. A rusty lock was attached to the door. Suddenly, they heard three knocks from inside. Knock. Knock. Knock. Everyone became silent. Raihan slowly moved closer to the door. Another three knocks followed. Then a woman's voice whispered, 'Please open the door.' One of Raihan's friends wanted to run away, but Raihan stayed there. The voice continued, 'I have been waiting for someone to open this door.' Raihan looked through the keyhole. He saw a woman standing in the darkness. Her face was pale, and her eyes were completely black. He immediately stepped backward. Suddenly, the lock on the door fell to the ground by itself. The door slowly opened. Nobody was standing inside. There was only an old wooden chair in the middle of the room. On the chair was an old photograph of a woman. Raihan picked it up and looked at the back. It said, 'My daughter, 1998–2014.' The next morning, Raihan asked the villagers about the woman. An old man told him that the owner's daughter had died in that room twelve years earlier. He also said something that made Raihan's blood run cold. 'The room has never been opened since the day she died.'

title: The Girl Who Asked for a Ride
text: Nabil was returning home on his motorcycle after attending a late-night gathering with his friends. It was around 12:30 AM, and the road was almost completely empty. There were no houses nearby, and the only light came from his motorcycle's headlamp. Suddenly, he noticed a young woman standing beside the road. She was wearing a long white dress and a red scarf. She raised her hand and asked for a ride. Nabil stopped because she looked frightened. He asked where she wanted to go. She quietly replied, 'Please take me to the old house near the cemetery.' Nabil felt slightly uncomfortable but agreed. The woman sat behind him. During the journey, she did not say anything. Nabil tried to start a conversation, but there was no response. After several minutes, he looked into the side mirror. He could see the woman's body, but he could not see her face. Her hair was completely covering it. Nabil became nervous and decided to stop the motorcycle. 'Are you okay?' he asked. There was no answer. He turned around. The woman was gone. The motorcycle was still moving, but the back seat was completely empty. Nabil immediately stopped and got off. Then he noticed two wet footprints on the seat. They were pointing toward him, as if someone had been standing directly behind him. He looked around but saw nobody. A few meters ahead was an old cemetery. Nabil walked toward it and noticed a small grave with a photograph attached to it. The photograph showed the same woman. Under it was written, 'Died on this road seven years ago.' Nabil ran back to his motorcycle. As he started the engine, he heard a woman's voice directly behind him. 'You forgot to take me home.' He never looked back. He drove as fast as he could until he reached the main road. When he finally stopped, he noticed something terrifying. The red scarf of the woman was hanging from his motorcycle mirror.

title: The Person in the Mirror
text: Tanvir had recently moved into a small house in a quiet mountain village. The house was cheap because nobody wanted to live there for long. The owner told Tanvir that the previous tenant had suddenly left without taking any of his belongings. Tanvir did not believe the rumors and moved in anyway. For the first few nights, everything seemed normal. Then he began noticing small strange things. Sometimes his bedroom door was open even though he clearly remembered closing it. Sometimes he heard footsteps outside his room. One night, at exactly 1:17 AM, Tanvir stood in front of the mirror while brushing his hair. He looked at his reflection and suddenly noticed something strange. When he stopped moving, the reflection continued moving for a few seconds. Tanvir became confused. He raised his right hand. The reflection raised its hand too, but several seconds later. He stepped away from the mirror. His reflection did not move. Instead, it simply stared at him. Tanvir felt a cold sensation running down his spine. Then the reflection smiled. Tanvir was not smiling. He slowly walked backward toward the door. The reflection placed both hands against the glass. A quiet voice came from inside the mirror. 'Don't be afraid.' Tanvir could hear his own voice, but it was coming from the reflection. 'I have been waiting for you.' Tanvir ran out of the room and called his neighbor. When they returned together, everything looked normal. The mirror was empty and Tanvir's reflection behaved normally. The next morning, Tanvir decided to remove the mirror from the wall. When he moved it, he found a small piece of paper hidden behind it. The paper contained only one sentence: 'The person you see in the mirror is not always you.' That night, Tanvir slept at his friend's house. The following morning, he received a photograph from the security camera inside his room. The photograph showed Tanvir standing in front of the mirror at 1:17 AM. But in the mirror, another person was standing behind him.

title: The Train That Never Arrived
text: There was an abandoned railway station outside the city that had been closed for more than twenty years. According to the local people, a terrible train accident had happened there many years ago. Several passengers had died, and the railway company eventually stopped using the station. Even after all those years, people living nearby claimed that a train could sometimes be heard arriving at exactly 12:05 AM. Arif and his two friends decided to investigate the story. They reached the station just before midnight. The platform was covered with weeds and dust. There were no lights except for the moon shining through the clouds. At exactly 12:05 AM, they heard a train whistle in the distance. The sound became louder. Soon, the ground started shaking. A bright light appeared at the end of the railway track. An old passenger train slowly entered the station. Arif could not believe his eyes. The train looked exactly like a train from decades ago. The doors opened, but nobody came out. Arif's friend raised his camera and started recording. Inside the train, dozens of passengers were sitting silently. None of them moved. Then one passenger slowly turned his head and looked directly at Arif. His face was covered with blood. Arif stepped backward in fear. Suddenly, every passenger inside the train turned toward him at the same time. His friends screamed and ran away. Arif followed them. They did not stop until they reached the main road. The next morning, they watched the video they had recorded. At first, everything looked normal. Then they noticed something strange. In the video, there were four people standing on the platform. Arif and his two friends were there, but another man was standing between them. It was the same bloody passenger from the train. At the end of the video, the man slowly turned toward the camera and whispered, 'The train is waiting for you.'

title: Someone Was Knocking
text: Imran lived alone in a small apartment in Dhaka. He worked during the day and usually returned home late at night. Everything was normal until one strange night when someone knocked on his door at exactly 3:33 AM. He looked through the peephole but could not see anyone. He waited for a few seconds, and then the knocking stopped. The following night, the same thing happened. Three knocks at exactly 3:33 AM. Knock. Knock. Knock. Imran started becoming nervous. On the third night, he decided to open the door. When the clock showed 3:33 AM, the knocking started again. He looked through the peephole. The hallway was empty. He opened the door slowly. Nobody was there. He stepped outside and looked in both directions. Suddenly, he heard a whisper from inside his apartment. 'Can you let me in?' Imran froze. He slowly turned around. At the end of the hallway inside his apartment stood a man who looked exactly like him. The other Imran was smiling. He raised his hand and waved. Real Imran slammed the door and ran downstairs. He called the building security guard and explained what had happened. When they returned to the apartment, nobody was there. Everything looked normal. The next morning, Imran decided to move out. While packing his belongings, he noticed something strange on his bedroom window. There were three wet fingerprints on the glass. The fingerprints were on the inside of the window. Imran touched them and realized they were exactly the same size as his own fingers. Then his phone suddenly received a message from an unknown number. The message contained only three words: 'Open the door.' The time on the message was 3:33 AM, even though it was still morning. Imran immediately left the apartment and never returned. The building was later demolished. But the security guard claimed that even after the building was gone, he sometimes heard three knocks at exactly 3:33 AM.
